style: A moonlit Nasreddin Hodja folktale told intimately at night. Natural cinematic English, low-key wonder, tactile physical effort, and dry humane comedy. Never sound like a cartoon, advertisement, or moral lesson. Preserve a small breath after each line and let the final joke land without a comic sting.

speakers.name: Narrator
speakers.style: An inviting older storyteller with a low textured voice, unhurried clarity, and quiet delight in Nasreddin's complete sincerity.

speakers.name: Nasreddin
speakers.style: An older man with dry warmth and absolute earnest conviction; his concern for the moon is sincere, his physical effort believable, and the humour never knowingly performed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Late one night, Nasreddin came to the well for water. Above the silent courtyard, a full moon kept watch.
lines.direction: Open quietly and spaciously; make the moon feel present before the problem begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He leaned over the rim. Far below, another moon trembled in the dark water.
lines.direction: Lean into the vertical distance and soften the final phrase with wonder.

lines.speaker: Nasreddin
lines.text: Mercy! The moon has fallen into the well!
lines.direction: A genuine shocked discovery, urgent but not shouted or played for comedy.

lines.speaker: Nasreddin
lines.text: Do not fear, old friend. I shall pull you out.
lines.direction: Tender reassurance followed by calm heroic resolve.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He tied an iron hook to a rope and lowered it carefully. The moon broke into silver rings around it.
lines.direction: Tactile and precise; leave visual room around silver rings.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At the bottom, the hook caught beneath a hidden stone. Nasreddin felt the rope go tight.
lines.direction: Quiet suspense, ending with a short firm emphasis on tight.

lines.speaker: Nasreddin
lines.text: I have you! Up you come…
lines.direction: Delighted certainty that turns into the first effort of pulling.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The stone would not let go. The rope drew tighter. Nasreddin braced one foot against the well and pulled with all his strength.
lines.direction: Build physical tension sentence by sentence without rushing the final effort.

lines.speaker: Nasreddin
lines.text: Just a little more! The world cannot go without its moon!
lines.direction: Breathless from effort, nobly determined, and completely sincere.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The rope snapped. Nasreddin flew backward and landed flat on his back. The moon in the well shattered into light.
lines.direction: Make the snap crisp, the fall physical, then slow into the beautiful water image.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Dazed, he opened his eyes. There was the moon—round, bright, and perfectly still in the sky.
lines.direction: Let the reveal arrive with relieved stillness and a tiny hidden smile.

lines.speaker: Nasreddin
lines.text: Praise be! My back may be bruised, but at least the moon is where it belongs.
lines.direction: Grateful, sore, and serenely satisfied; never signal that he understands the mistake.
